A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same surrogate-loss framework and experimental program. Their main text, equations, figures, algorithms, and Appendices A–E are available and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on hidden games, a 100-state Markov chain, and Ant/HalfCheetah policy evaluation, including additional experiments in Appendices C and D.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results, revises the online policy-evaluation curves, and adds a 16-layer network experiment in Appendix D.2.1.

M1.justification: The surrogate objective, alpha-descent condition, Algorithm 1, Section 4 update rules, and TD variants in Algorithms 2–4 remain unchanged. The deeper network is an additional evaluation configuration, not a revised optimization method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate hidden matching pennies, hidden rock-paper-scissors, the 100-state Markov chain, and Ant/HalfCheetah policy evaluation, including offline full-batch evaluation. The added network-depth experiment reuses existing tasks and environments.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain PHGD, GDA, GN, DGN, LM, and the surrogate variants, with TD(0) retained in the nonlinear experiments. Figure 10 uses the existing comparator set. The new least-squares policy-evaluation citation does not introduce another evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix D.2.1 adds evaluation with a 16-layer MLP alongside the existing two-layer network. Section 5.2.2 also changes the reported reference-value approximation from 100 to 10 Monte Carlo roll-outs. The PDFs establish a reported setting change without explaining whether it reflects rerunning experiments or correcting documentation.

E4.justification: The new larger-network experiment in Appendix D.2.1 and Figure 10 checks sensitivity of performance and runtime to network depth. The existing inner-step comparisons, random-initialization analyses, and offline Bellman-gap experiments are retained.

E5.justification: The Monte Carlo reference-value estimator changes its reported sampling budget from 100 to 10 roll-outs in Section 5.2.2. Training-run uncertainty reporting remains unchanged: nonlinear results use 20 runs and 95% confidence intervals, including the added Figure 10.

E6.justification: Figure 4 contains revised Ant/HalfCheetah prediction-error trajectories and error levels. Figure 10 adds 16-layer results, described as having similar runtime and performance to the two-layer case. Figures 1–3 and 5–9 retain their results. The changed reported roll-out budget prevents treating the updated errors as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.2 makes the previously derived contraction factor explicit and adds a concrete parameter choice yielding rate 1 - mu^2/(5L^2). This replaces the separate alpha <= C eta^p alternative and its appendix derivation. The main assumptions, stochastic convergence result, and divergence counterexample remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: convergence under hidden structure and sufficient surrogate descent, optimizer compatibility, unification of preconditioning methods, and efficient TD variants. The added evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: The explanations of double-sampling bias and variance, inner-loop computational tradeoffs, convexity/interpolation requirements, and limitations of inner-loop guarantees are retained. The new depth passage reports comparable performance without adding a substantive mechanism explanation or limitation.

D1.justification: Section 5.2.2 newly specifies 10,000 test states but removes v1's explicit statement that the online surrogate methods use AdamW. The appendix still specifies AdamW for estimating the offline Bellman-gap infimum. This changes reproducibility information without establishing an optimizer switch.

R1.justification: v3 adds Bertsekas and Ioffe (1996) and identifies the retained stochastic update with least-squares policy evaluation. It also clarifies where the boundedness assumption enters the cited Sakos analysis and removes the Loshchilov (2017) reference. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Localized edits refine operator terminology from smooth to Lipschitz, shorten or rename headings, expand a footnote, and add the short larger-network subsection. The publication header and acknowledgments change, while the overall narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 10, makes Figure 4 more compact with revised axis ranges, and relocates appendix figures. Resizing and reflow around Figure 2 remove the caption/body-text overlap visible in v1. The overall visual organization is retained.

improvement.justification: The explicit parameter/rate guarantee in Theorem 3.2, added network-depth check, and repair of Figure 2's caption overlap improve clarity and empirical support. These gains are limited by sparse documentation of the deeper-network experiment and removal of the online AdamW disclosure. The revised Figure 4 and changed roll-out budget do not establish a between-version performance improvement.
